title: termguicolors + underline/bold: garbage escape sequence chars

labels.name: bug-regression
labels.description: wrong behavior that was introduced in a previous commit (please bisect)

body:
<!-- Before reporting: search existing issues and check the FAQ. -->

- `nvim --version`: NVIM v0.2.1-dev
- `dpkg -l | grep neovim`: 0.2.0ubuntu1+git201710092056+3676+26~ubuntu16.04.1
- Vim (version: ) behaves differently? Yes.
- Operating system/version: Ubuntu 16.04
- Terminal name/version: gnome-terminal/3.18.3-1ubuntu1, xterm/322-1ubuntu1
- `$TERM`: xterm-256color
- `$COLORTERM`: gnome-terminal

### Steps to reproduce using minimal `.vimrc` + minimal `.vim`
(edit 1: Add dependency on ~/.vim/after/syntax/c.vim)
(edit 2: Removed dependency on any plugin/colorscheme)

* The minimal `.vimrc`:
``` vim
if has('nvim')
  set termguicolors
endif
hi! Normal gui=NONE cterm=NONE guifg=#657b83 ctermfg=11 guibg=#fdf6e3 ctermbg=15
hi! MatchParen gui=NONE,underline,bold cterm=NONE,underline,bold guifg=#dc322f ctermfg=1 guibg=#eee8d5 ctermbg=7
" The 2 following lines here or in ~/.vim/after/syntax/c.vim
syn match cBraces display "[{}]"
hi def link cBraces Delimiter
```
Optionally, the last 2 lines above can be moved into `~/.vim/after/syntax/c.vim`.

* Create a file named `tmp.c`, containing 128 lines full of stuff, like:
``` bash
for((j=0;j<128;j++)); do echo "{ $(for((i=0;i<17;i++)); do echo -n '0x00, '; done) }"; done > tmp.c
```

* Maximize terminal window (it must display at least 50 lines or such).

* Edit the file:
```
nvim tmp.c
```

### Actual behaviour

We see garbage (escape sequence character):
* In xterm:
```
{ 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, }
{ 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, [?25l255m0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, }
{ 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, }
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16546024/31531596-484f33c2-afe8-11e7-8f89-0b33411fbe4c.png)

* In gnome-terminal:
```
40 { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, }
41 { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00?38:2:101:123:131m, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, }
42 { 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, }
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16546024/31531460-8b3e4200-afe7-11e7-9151-d6e98ad7d9bd.png)
The garbage appears in black when using file `.vim/after/syntax/c.vim`. Otherwise it will appear in the same color as surrounding text.

### Expected behaviour

There should be no garbage character

### Analysis
* The garbage is always at the same position.
* The bug does not occur when reducing the number of characters on the line. For instance, the bug disappear if we use `i<16` in the bash line to generate tmp.c. But it comes back with `i<16` when using `set numbers` for instance. So it looks like an overflow bug.
* The bug does not occur when removing the last line in minimal .vimrc, or removing `underline` like in:
```
hi! MatchParen gui=NONE,bold cterm=NONE,bold guifg=#dc322f ctermfg=1 guibg=#eee8d5 ctermbg=7
```
